title: TS hybrid consumer pattern for SDK streaming (async-iterator <> Web Streams)
creator: Marcos Rivera
description: Introduce a "hybrid consumer" abstraction in the TypeScript SDK that allows a single streaming response to be consumed ergonomically as either an AsyncIterator or a Web ReadableStream with correct backpressure, cancellation propagation, and retry/resume semantics.
background: Current SDK streaming helpers provide separate adapters for AsyncIterator and Web Streams but force callers to choose one shape up-front. Real apps sometimes need to expose the same streaming source to multiple runtimes: server-side code prefers async iterators, browser app code prefers ReadableStream, and middleware (proxies, observability) often needs to tap into the stream. Existing tickets covered adapters and pipes, but we still see friction around resuming after partial failures, preserving prefix caching, and ensuring predictable backpressure across both consumption models.
motivation: Reduce duplication and user confusion by exposing a single, well-documented primitive that safely supports both consumption styles (one active consumer at a time), clear cancellation semantics, and a resume token API to support retries without re-rendering from scratch. Aim to cut customer support requests about flaky stream resumption and mismatched memory/backpressure behavior.
design_summary: Implement a lightweight 'HybridStream' wrapper that sits on top of the existing SDK response stream. The wrapper exposes three helpers: .asAsyncIterator(), .asReadableStream(), and .snapshotResumeToken(). Only one active consumer is allowed; attempting to create a second active consumer throws. Cancellation from either side signals the underlying transport. When a transient network error occurs, the SDK can call .resume(resumeToken) to continue generation from the last emitted token (if the model/endpoint supports it). The wrapper bridges backpressure by translating ReadableStream pull/close into iterator next() pacing and vice-versa. We'll provide two public factory helpers: createHybridStream(response) and createHybridFromGenerator(asyncGeneratorFn, options) for advanced usage.
api_proposals: resume(token: string): Promise<boolean> // returns true if resume successful
export function createHybridStream<T>(source: ResponseLike, opts?: {enableResume?: boolean, bufferThreshold?: number}): HybridStream<T>
implementation_steps: 1) Design TypeScript types and internal state machine (idle, consumed-by-iterator, consumed-by-readable, cancelled, resumed).
2) Implement a win32-friendly shim that maps AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream and vice-versa using an internal ring buffer with configurable soft limit (bufferThreshold).
3) Hook cancellation tokens into existing transport layer (fetch AbortController / node-fetch / undici) so cancel() aborts the HTTP request and frees KV-prefetch caches.
4) Implement snapshotResumeToken() by capturing model-level last-emitted token/offset when the model/endpoint supports it; add SDK no-op when resume not supported.
5) Add public docs and examples (README + console quickstart snippet) and update CHANGELOG.
6) Add unit + integration tests and a small TS playground example that runs in browser & node.
7) Performance test: measure memory under high-concurrency workloads; iterate on bufferThreshold defaults.
8) Release behind opt-in flag first (experimental.hybridStreaming=true) for 2 cycles before GA.
testing_plan: Unit tests: consumer switch enforcement (cannot have two active consumers).
Unit tests: cancellation from iterator cancels readable reader and underlying transport.
Integration test: resume() successfully continues when server-side resume token supported (mock server).
Browser compatibility test: ReadableStream returned is spec-compliant in Chromium and WebKit.
Stress test: 1k concurrent hybrid streams with bursty consumption to validate bufferThreshold and memory usage.
End-to-end scenario: server SSE -> node consumer -> browser consumer migrated to readable stream in a proxy scenario.
Observability: add debug logs for state transitions and emit telemetry for resume attempts (success/failure).
acceptance_criteria: Public API shipped behind experimental flag with docs and examples.
Unit and integration tests pass in CI and coverage for new module >= 90%.
Memory regression: <10% overhead vs existing adapter when no resume enabled.
Interop tests: async iterator -> readable -> async iterator roundtrip works without data duplication or loss.
A small set of internal customers (console streaming, examples repo, infra-runbooks) have validated the ergonomics and provided sign-off.
Feature gate documented and rollout plan created for GA.
Telemetry for resume attempts appears in dev/staging dashboards.
No regressions in existing TS streaming tests (run full SDK test-suite).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Multiple consumers attempt to read concurrently -> we enforce single active consumer and provide clear runtime error message and migration guidance.
Risk: Mis-translating backpressure semantics causes memory blowups -> mitigate by conservative default bufferThreshold and observability metrics; add an opt-in low-latency mode.
Risk: Resume tokens are not universally supported by all models/endpoints -> resume is opt-in; the API is a best-effort boolean and SDK provides a deterministic fallback path.
Risk: Edge cases across bundlers (polyfills for ReadableStream) -> ship lightweight polyfill detection and test with common bundlers (esbuild, webpack, rollup).
Risk: Cancellation races between user code and SDK re-tries -> introduce state machine and idempotent cancel semantics; add tests for races.
Mitigation: initial release behind feature flag, gather metrics, iterate.
Mitigation: include migration doc for users currently using separate adapter helpers.
Mitigation: provide a small helper utils package snippet for common patterns (sseToReadable, iteratorToReadable) but mark internal-only until GA.
notes: Related tickets: ENG-27158 (stream union shim), ENG-40567 (bridge backpressure scenarios). Those focused on specific adapter edges; this ticket centralizes the consumer-facing surface with explicit resume semantics.
We should coordinate with documentation (DevEx) to provide both server-side and browser examples and a migration guide for customers currently using the legacy stream adapters.
Consider adding a telemetry label 'hybrid_stream' for tracking early usage and failures; limit PII in telemetry.
If successful, consider equivalent helpers in Python SDK (async generator <-> trio/anyio streams) and Go (chan <> io.Reader).
Accounting for Node JSX servers: ensure the hybrid ReadableStream plays nicely with Response streaming in Next.js/Edge runtimes.
Design note: do not try to support multiple simultaneous readers; if customers need tap-like functionality, recommend explicit tee() with documented caveats.
Prototype implemented in a feature branch: feature/hybrid-streaming-2025-02 (internal PR will follow).
